title: How Does Sunlight Become Electricity? ☀️
description: Solar panels have no moving parts, yet they make electricity! See how sunlight knocks electrons loose inside silicon and powers your home.

scenes.say: A solar panel has no moving parts, yet it makes electricity from sunlight. How?

scenes.caption: Silicon cells
scenes.say: The panel is made of cells of silicon, the same element found in sand, but specially treated.
When sunlight hits a cell, it knocks electrons loose. The cell is built in two layers that push those electrons in one direction, and that flow is an electric current.

scenes.caption: The inverter
scenes.say: But this is direct current, and your home uses alternating current, so a device called an inverter converts it.

scenes.label: Becomes electricity in home panels
scenes.say: Today's home panels turn roughly twenty percent of the sunlight that hits them into electricity.
